# The drag-arm timer can decline its own delay by a millisecond

## Context

`dev`'s unit job at `7214b9249e` (job 128897902188) failed `Pointer.spec.mjs:638`, "holding still past touchDelay arms the drag", with `Expected: 1 · Received: 0 · Timeout 5000ms exceeded`. The retry passed. Ada caught it in a defect-note. #20625 (for #20624) had replaced that test's fixed 40 ms sleep with an `expect.poll` on `drag:start`. With a 10 ms `touchDelay` and a 5 s poll, the drag did not start late: it never started.

## The Problem

`onPointerDown` arms `pointerDownTimeout = setTimeout(() => onDistanceChange({...point, pointerId}), delay)`. The callback re-measures `Date.now() - pointerDownTime >= delay`. The timer runs on a monotonic clock, while `Date.now()` floors the wall clock at different millisecond boundaries, so a timer that fires on time can read `delay - 1`. The check then declines, nothing re-arms, and a pointer held still never starts its drag. A moving pointer recovers, because each `pointermove` checks again, so a real finger's jitter mostly hides the defect. The unit test holds perfectly still and fails outright.

Measured, Node 25 on darwin: 11 of 1,500 10 ms timers fired while `Date.now()` showed less than 10 ms elapsed.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/main/draggable/sensor/Pointer.mjs`, `onPointerDown`, sets the timer for both paths: touch reads `touchDelay` and mouse reads `delay` (`getThresholds`).
- `onDistanceChange` is both the timer's re-entry and the `pointermove` listener before the threshold. Only the timer knows its delay has elapsed.

## The Fix

`onDistanceChange(event, delayElapsed=false)`: the timeout calls it with `true`, and the arm condition reads `(delayElapsed || timeElapsed >= delay) && distanceTravelled >= minDistance`. The `pointermove` path keeps measuring, and the distance threshold is unchanged.

Decision Record impact: none.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A touch held still arms its drag when the timer fires, even with `Date.now()` one millisecond short of the delay. A unit test stubs `Date.now` to read the delay 1 ms short; it fails before the fix and passes after.
- [ ] The Pointer sensor's existing specs pass.

## Out of Scope

- The distance threshold, the mouse `delay` default, and the `pointermove` arming path.
- The test's poll from #20625 stays: it waits on the event, not on time.
